name: Fesoterodine pivotal trials
question: Do fixed doses of fesoterodine improve overactive bladder symptoms compared with placebo?

design.population: Adults with increased micturition frequency and urgency, with or without urgency urinary incontinence.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled randomized trial
design.locator: Chapple PubMed abstract, Methods; FDA medical review, p 2, Study SP583

verdictNote: Both fixed fesoterodine doses improved the primary and coprimary outcomes versus placebo.
takeaway: In the Chapple pivotal trial, fesoterodine 4 mg and 8 mg once daily improved micturition frequency, urgency urinary incontinence, and treatment response over placebo at 12 weeks; tolterodine ER was an active control.

reports.label: International pivotal trial (SP583)
reports.citation: Chapple C, Van Kerrebroeck P, Tubaro A, et al. "Clinical efficacy, safety, and tolerability of once-daily fesoterodine in subjects with overactive bladder." *Eur Urol.* 2007;52(4):1204-1212. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2007.07.009

results.measure: Mean change from baseline to week 12
results.note: P<0.001 for each fesoterodine dose versus placebo; FDA-reproduced sponsor results, last observation carried forward.
results.locator: FDA medical review, p 3, Table 1, Study SP583

results.endpoint: Urgency urinary incontinence episodes per 24 hours
results.measure: Mean change from baseline to week 12 among participants incontinent at baseline
results.note: P=0.001 for 4 mg and P<0.001 for 8 mg versus placebo; FDA-reproduced sponsor results.
results.locator: FDA medical review, p 3, Table 2, Study SP583

results.note: The abstract gives no response proportions or dose-specific P values.
results.locator: Chapple PubMed abstract, Methods and Results

delivery.label: Fixed-dose treatment
delivery.value: Fesoterodine 4 mg or 8 mg, tolterodine ER 4 mg, or placebo once daily for 12 weeks.

reports.label: Separate US pivotal trial (SP584)
reports.citation: Nitti VW, Dmochowski R, Sand PK, et al. "Efficacy, safety and tolerability of fesoterodine for overactive bladder syndrome." *J Urol.* 2007;178(6):2488-2494. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2007.08.033

results.measure: Mean change from baseline to week 12
results.note: P=0.032 for 4 mg and P<0.001 for 8 mg versus placebo; FDA-reproduced sponsor results.
results.locator: FDA medical review, p 3, Table 1, Study SP584

results.endpoint: Urgency urinary incontinence episodes per 24 hours
results.measure: Mean change from baseline to week 12 among participants incontinent at baseline
results.note: P=0.002 for 4 mg and P<0.001 for 8 mg versus placebo; FDA-reproduced sponsor results.
results.locator: FDA medical review, p 3, Table 2, Study SP584

results.note: The abstract gives no response proportions or dose-specific P values.
results.locator: Nitti PubMed abstract, Materials and Methods and Results

harms.label: Dry mouth, constipation, and urinary tract infection
harms.note: The abstract does not provide event rates or separate the two fesoterodine doses.

delivery.label: US trial treatment
delivery.value: Fesoterodine 4 mg (283 randomized), fesoterodine 8 mg (279), or placebo (274) once daily for 12 weeks; 836 total randomized.
delivery.locator: Nitti PubMed abstract, Materials and Methods

reports.label: Pooled open-label extensions
reports.citation: Scarpero H, Sand PK, Kelleher CJ, et al. "Long-term safety, tolerability, and efficacy of fesoterodine treatment in men and women with overactive bladder symptoms." *Curr Med Res Opin.* 2011;27(5):921-930. doi:10.1185/03007995.2011.559581
reports.followUp: Open-label treatment assessed through 24 months; maximum allowed 24-36 months
reports.followUpLocator: PubMed abstract, Research Design and Methods and Main Outcome Measures

results.measure: Change from double-blind baseline through open-label month 24
results.note: In pooled flexible-dose extension participants followed through month 24, improvements were sustained or further improved. Open-label extensions pooled participants from SP583 and SP584; all began at 8 mg, with dose reduction and re-escalation permitted.
results.locator: Scarpero PubMed abstract, Research Design and Methods and Results

harms.label: Dry mouth in pooled flexible-dose extension
harms.note: All participants began at 8 mg; annual dose reduction to 4 mg and re-escalation were permitted. Rates are by sex, not randomized dose.

delivery.label: Continuation through 24 months
delivery.value: 83/185 men (45%) and 356/705 women (50%) continued open-label fesoterodine for at least 24 months.
